subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should isolated cron setup be allowed to use a bounded share of the job timeout budget instead of the current fixed 60s setup watchdog?
rationale: The source fix is narrow and proof-positive, but it intentionally changes cron availability behavior by allowing slow or stuck setup to occupy cron capacity longer before aborting.

options.title: Land the bounded setup-budget fix
options.body: Accept the longer capped setup window in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219 and keep the issue open only until that PR lands or is replaced.

options.title: Keep the 60s hard cap
options.body: Leave current behavior in place and document staggered schedules, command cron jobs, or provider/runtime-specific fixes as the supported mitigation.

options.title: Ask for a config-first design
options.body: Require a maintainer-approved config or doctor path before changing the default setup watchdog budget.

recommendation.title: Land the bounded setup-budget fix
recommendation.body: Accept the longer capped setup window in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219 and keep the issue open only until that PR lands or is replaced.

likelyOwner.reason: He carried the prior cron watchdog fixes and related closeout decisions, so he is the strongest current routing candidate for the timeout-policy tradeoff.
